prerequisites: Successful completion of modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know and can explain the essential mass transport mechanisms and forms.
Students can describe various transport processes and equilibria in multiphase systems and their interactions.
Students are able to qualitatively and quantitatively analyze concrete case examples of mass transfer in single-phase and multiphase systems.
Students can correctly use and clearly explain in their own words the concepts of thermodynamic equilibrium, chemical kinetics, and electrochemistry.
Students are able to apply thermodynamic methodology for calculating state properties and state changes of multicomponent systems.
Students are able to practically apply the course content using calculation examples, independently develop solutions, present their results on the board, and discuss them orally.
Students acquire foreign language competence by using English textbooks.

syllabus_topics: Thermal and calorimetric properties of mixtures
Equations of state from molecular thermodynamics
Modeling and calculation of phase equilibria
Chemical potential in mixtures of ideal gases
Phase equilibrium models for other cases
Temperature and pressure dependence of thermodynamic state variables
assessment_rules: The module completion examination consists of a written exam of 120-180 minutes, which accounts for 100% of the module grade. Performance points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
